news.title: FAA orders third nationwide ground stop in its history
paras: Grounded FAA orders third nationwide ground stop in its history Rare nationwide ground stop could go on for awhile as FAA troubleshoots. Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy announced the ground stop on X , citing a “communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers.” Duffy promised updates as more information is known and said FAA staff were troubleshooting the problem.

Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said that the ground stop was not prompted by a security threat. “This is a telecommunications outage out of the FAA. Out of an abundance of caution, we have grounded all of the flights,” Mullin said .

news.title: Millions of Americans are not taking their GLP-1 drugs as prescribed
paras: Real-world use Millions of Americans are not taking their GLP-1 drugs as prescribed Cost and access barriers are pushing people to modified use and unapproved versions. Woman using an obesity drug injection pen.

The peptide-based drugs are both highly effective and wildly popular for diabetes, weight loss and a growing range of connected chronic health conditions, including cardiovascular disease and obstructive sleep apnea. But, amid the boom, the latest data suggests millions of Americans have turned to unapproved versions and are using the potent drugs in ways doctors never intended, raising questions about what that real-world use means for safety and efficacy.

news.title: In elephants, the resilience of communities has its limits
paras: Network problems In elephants, the resilience of communities has its limits In Sri Lanka, ecological change is shrinking a park’s elephant population. Individuals die or move away, calves grow up, and newcomers join, but the local communities as a whole usually hold together.

Long-term studies of African savanna elephants have shown that, even after poaching or other spikes in deaths, survivors tend to rebuild their lost connections over time. But a new study suggests that resilience may not keep the community intact when steady losses accumulate over time. Anastasia Madsen, a behavioral ecologist at the University of California, San Diego, and her colleagues analyzed 12 years of observations of wild Asian elephants in Sri Lanka.

news.title: California's brand-new Air & Space Center, home of the space shuttle Endeavour, opens today
paras: Welcome to the Samuel Oschin Air & Space Center at the California Science Center. After more than three decades in development, folks can finally visit the Los Angeles science museum's massive new wing.

For most of us, the biggest draw is its centerpiece: the retired space shuttle Endeavour , sitting upright in launch position, towering at nearly 200 feet (61 meters) tall. "It just takes your breath away when you see that reveal and the doors open and you get to look at it for the first time. news.title: 'Arrival' at 10: Denis Villeneuve's alien visitation classic that reminded us it's good to talk
paras: How the 'Dune' director turned a little-known short story into one of the best sci-fi movies of the 21st century In " Star Trek ", universal translators come as standard, while C-3PO has spent the last 49 years reminding everyone in "Star Wars" that he's fluent in over six million forms of communication.

But in "Arrival" — which was released 10 years ago in November 2016 — making first contact proves to be rather more challenging than maintaining your Duolingo streak. In fact, working out how to establish a dialogue with extraterrestrial visitors becomes the whole point of this powerful and heartbreaking story, as the fate of planet Earth hinges on the interpretation of a single noun.

news.title: Two Centuries After This Bronze Leg Emerged From a Scottish Bog, Archaeologists Believe It May Have Belonged t
paras: Add as preferred source Curator Fraser Hunter examines the bronze leg. Duncan McGlynn In 1820, a larger-than-life gilded bronze lower leg was pulled out of a bog in the Scottish Borders region.

For more than two centuries, historians discredited the idea that the Roman-era artifact came from Scotland, instead assuming that it was hacked off a monument in England and hauled north by marauding tribes. Instead, they posit that it formed part of a colossal equestrian statue of the Roman Emperor Antoninus Pius that once stood in southern Scotland in the second century C.E., before it was dismantled by retreating Roman troops.

sport.title: Andreeva sweeps WTA Finals group losing just 11 games, brushing aside stand-in Shnaider
paras: Mirra Andreeva beat alternate Diana Shnaider 6-2, 6-1 in 55 minutes to complete a perfect group stage at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells: three wins, six sets, 11 games dropped. She faces Jessica Pegula in the semi-finals on Saturday.

Mirra Andreeva completed a perfect group stage at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells on Friday. The third seed beat her compatriot and doubles partner Diana Shnaider 6-2, 6-1 in 55 minutes, and ends Group 2 with three wins, six sets won and only 11 games dropped. Andreeva converted six of her seven break points against Shnaider, who had stepped in as second alternate after Karolina Muchova withdrew with gastrointestinal issues.

sport.title: Every player who beat Rafael Nadal at the ATP Finals after failing to win the title in his 11 appearances
paras: Rafael Nadal was never able to win a single title at the ATP Finals in his career. Nadal is considered one of the greatest tennis players of all time as a former world number one, who won 22 Grand Slam titles, 36 Masters 1000 tournaments and Olympic gold medals in both singles and doubles.

However, one of the tournaments Nadal never won in his career was the ATP Finals , despite his biggest rivals Novak Djokovic and Roger Federer having won 13 titles at the tournament. Nadal qualified for the ATP Finals 17 times in his career, but actually competed at the year-end tournament 11 times, but he was never able to walk away with the title.
